title: Your tongue tip: /t/ and /d/
goal: Practise /t/ and /d/ and use it in a short, understandable exchange.
cue: Touch the ridge just behind your upper front teeth with your tongue tip, then release. Initial stressed t usually has a stronger puff than d.
spelling: t and d represent different sounds. In natural American speech, some middle t and d sounds are very similar; today practise word beginnings.
task: Say how many tickets you need. Ask the other person to confirm the number.
story: Ben has two red pens. One pen is on the desk.
storyQuestion: How many pens does Ben have?
reviewPrompt: Return to day 1, 8, 12, 14. Recall a word or say one useful phrase before opening those lessons.

articulation.label: mat
articulation.alt: mat: /m/ → /æ/ → /t/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
notes: /m/: Close both lips; air goes through the nose.
/æ/: Low front tongue; open the jaw.
/t/: Tongue tip touches the ridge, then releases.
articulation.note: Join the sounds smoothly after practising each position.
